# Search

Optimisation over a space you can only sample. You say how to make a genome and how to vary one, you say what a genome scored, and a driver spends a budget of *evaluations* against that pair. Nothing in the drivers knows what a genome is, so it can be a cellular-automaton rule, an L-system, an `Fn` graph or a design vector. One file holds all five: random sampling, hill climbing, a (µ+λ) evolutionary loop, novelty search and MAP-Elites. The callers are on three other pages: [ALife](alife.md) evolves rules and L-systems, [Function](function.md) evolves function graphs, and [Simulation](simulation.md)'s `KratosStudy` searches a design space. `afield.lang.morpho` keeps a search of its own. Read `PopulationSearch.kt` for why `random` is reported as a control arm, and why the budget is evaluations rather than generations: both decide whether a result means anything.

## ColorRpn.kt { #colorrpn-kt }

A reverse-Polish language whose programs are pictures: tokens push numbers and colours onto a
stack, the program runs once per pixel of a square, and what is left on the stack is that
pixel's colour.

[`ColorRpn`](search.md#colorrpn-kt-colorrpn) is the language, and it is small enough to read in one sitting: four variables for
where the pixel is, twenty-five words, and no way to fail. Compiling a program gives a
[`ColorRpnProgram`](search.md#colorrpn-kt-colorrpnprogram), which reports the colour at one point, renders a square at any size on all
cores, or hands back PNG bytes that `display` shows as an image.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
display("main", ColorRpn.compile("x 9 * sin 0.18 +  y 0.55 +  0.62  hsl").png(256))
```

The rest of the family builds a search on top: `ColorRpnGenome.kt` breeds one program from two,
and `ColorRpnEvolution.kt` puts a grid of the results in a box for you to pick from. The
language is described word by word on [`ColorRpn`](search.md#colorrpn-kt-colorrpn) below.

### ColorRpn { #colorrpn-kt-colorrpn }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">ColorRpn</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/rpn/ColorRpn/#L87)

The colour expression language of the madp *GA* demo (`ga.html`): a reverse-Polish program run once per pixel, whose result is a colour. It is the genome of interactive evolution in the manner of Karl Sims' *Genetic Images* (see `ColorRpnGenome` and `afield.study.search.EyeEvolution`), and this file follows the demo's interpreter exactly, so a program draws the same picture here as in the browser.

## ColorRpnEvolution.kt { #colorrpnevolution-kt }

The box-facing front of the [`ColorRpn`](search.md#colorrpn-kt-colorrpn) family: one call puts a breeding grid of generated
pictures in a box's output panel, and clicking two of them breeds the next generation.

[`colorRpnEvolution`](search.md#colorrpnevolution-kt--colorrpnevolution) is the three other files joined up, with the madp GA demo's choices filled
in: [`ColorRpn`](search.md#colorrpn-kt-colorrpn) as the genome, [`ColorRpnGenome`](search.md#colorrpngenome-kt-colorrpngenome) as the breeding, `EyeEvolution.kt`'s grid as the
interface, and a toolbar over the breeding knobs that are worth turning while you watch. Call
`afield.study.search.evolveByEye` directly instead when you want to change any of that.

## ColorRpnGenome.kt { #colorrpngenome-kt }

The breeding rules for [`ColorRpn`](search.md#colorrpn-kt-colorrpn) programs: what a child of two programs is, and the eight
mutations that make one.

[`ColorRpnBreeding`](search.md#colorrpngenome-kt-colorrpnbreeding) is the knobs, with the madp GA demo's values as the defaults: how many
mutations a child gets, the length it is nudged toward, the chance of splicing a slice out of
the other parent, and how often each of the eight mutations is chosen. [`ColorRpnGenome`](search.md#colorrpngenome-kt-colorrpngenome) applies
them, and because it implements [`GenomeOps`](search.md#populationsearch-kt-genomeops) the same genome drives both halves of
`afield.study.search`: the picture grid of `EyeEvolution.kt`, where you pick the parents, and
the scored drivers of `PopulationSearch.kt`, where an [`Objective`](search.md#populationsearch-kt-objective) picks them.

A mutation can produce a program that makes no sense, and nothing rejects it. [`ColorRpn`](search.md#colorrpn-kt-colorrpn) reads
any token sequence as some picture, which is what lets a search of this space run without a
validity test.

## StackSLEvolution.kt { #stackslevolution-kt }

The resumable StackSL search: [`StackSLEvolution`](search.md#stackslevolution-kt-stackslevolution) holds the island populations, the stage
schedule and the per-origin credit table between generations, and saves them as a
[`StackSLEvolutionSnapshot`](search.md#stackslevolution-kt-stackslevolutionsnapshot).

The settings ([`StackSLEvolveSettings`](search.md#stackslevolution-kt-stackslevolvesettings), [`StackSLStage`](search.md#stackslevolution-kt-stackslstage)), the history records and the
[`StackSLPopulationArchive`](search.md#stackslevolution-kt-stackslpopulationarchive) that files snapshots on disk live here too.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolution.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolution/)

**Used in:** [Evolving a Shader Toward a Picture](../stacksl_evolve.md)

A program the destination already has is not copied. |

## StackSLEvolve.kt { #stackslevolve-kt }

Genetic programming over StackSL **token sequences**, scored by rendering the program and
comparing it to a target image.

This is a third shape of consumer for `PopulationSearch.kt`. The two that were there before it
evolve *numbers or rule tables* — `FunctionEvolve.kt` mutates an `Fn` expression graph and
`alife_evolve.kt` mutates rule tables, growth windows and grammar bodies — and neither has a
phenotype you can look at. Here the genome is a program in a real language, the phenotype is a
picture, and the thing in between is the production emitter plus `afield.lang.stacksl.cpu`'s
interpreter. Nothing about what a StackSL word *means* is restated in this file.

### What is new here and what is not

Being precise about this, because three of the four ingredients already existed:

 - **Not new: linear-genome GP with this operator set.** `LSystemGenome` in `alife_evolve.kt`
   already has `point`, `insert`, `delete`, `duplicate`, `swap`, single-point crossover and a
   `signature`, over a string of turtle symbols. [`StackSLGenome`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt-stackslgenome)'s operators are that set,
   lifted to a token list, and the resemblance is deliberate.
 - **Not new: synthesising a program as text and letting a real compiler judge it.**
   `afield.lang.morpho.MorphoGenome` does exactly that for MorphoHDL, and already reports its invalid
   fraction rather than hiding it. It predates `PopulationSearch` and runs on a private search
   core.
 - **New: the phenotype is an image**, produced by the same emitter a GPU reads, so fitness is a
   measurement of a rendered picture rather than of a scalar or a netlist.
 - **New: a program-text genome on the *generic* core**, so [`PopulationSearch.random`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--populationsearch--random),
   [`PopulationSearch.evolve`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--populationsearch--evolve), [`PopulationSearch.novelty`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--populationsearch--novelty), [`PopulationSearch.mapElites`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--populationsearch--mapelites) and
   `Selection.LEXICASE` are all available to it without any of them being written again.

### Arity: there was nothing to repair and nothing to reject

The plan this file was written against asked for a deliberate choice between *repairing* a token
sequence into a legal stack effect and *rejecting* it as invalid. Measured against the real
compiler, that is a false dichotomy for a straight-line program: **StackSL has no invalid
straight-line programs.** `StackSLCompileOptions.defaultValues` fills any operand the stack does
not have, and it does so *without* an ERROR diagnostic even at `tolerant = false` — `+` on its
own compiles, `ok`, and leaves the stack at depth 1. The silent-pruning hazard that
`finalStackDepth` exists to expose belongs to **definitions** (`: name … ;`), whose arity has to
work out for the emitted function to be called at all; this generator emits no definitions, so
it cannot hit it.

So [`StackSLGenome`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt-stackslgenome) does not repair for validity and does not reject. It carries a *model* of
each word's stack effect ([`StackSLWord.consumes`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslword--consumes)) and uses it only to **steer** generation — the
same relationship `MorphoWidthModel` has to MorphoHDL's real width inference, where "the compiler
remains the judge; the model's accuracy shows up as `failureRate` and nowhere else". Here the
model's accuracy shows up as [`StackSLEvolveRun.danglingValues`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslevolverun--danglingvalues), which counts values a program
pushed and never consumed, read off the compiler's own analysis.

### The gate that actually matters is on the image, not on the program

A program that compiles perfectly and renders a flat grey rectangle is the single most likely way
a search like this produces a fake result: two blanks agree with each other everywhere, and a
plain error metric will happily rank one of them first. [`StackSLImageObjective`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt-stackslimageobjective) therefore scores
a constant-colour render as invalid, inside the fitness function, and refuses a target that is
itself blank.

### Beating chance is not resembling the target

The first version of this file scored `1 -` mean absolute RGB error, now `StackSLMetric.PIXEL`.
Evolution beat the random control on four of five targets under it, and the pictures mostly did
not look like their targets: a yellow disc evolved into dark diagonal streaks, four quadrants
into a vertical gradient. An absolute error is satisfied first by matching the target's overall
colour balance, and the search found that rather than the layout. `StackSLMetric.LPIPS`, the
default, scores with a learned perceptual distance instead ([`afield.ai.inference.onnx.Lpips`](machine-learning.md#lpips-kt-lpips)).
[`StackSLLayout.layoutAgreement`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stacksllayout--layoutagreement) is the independent check on whether a result resembles its
target, and `StackSLEvolveGallery.figureTargets` runs both metrics against each other and asserts
on it.

### Cost, so the budget is chosen rather than discovered

One 32x32 candidate is about 1,000 pixel-shader invocations through `afield.lang.stacksl.cpu`'s
interpreter, which runs 1.3–1.6 x 10^4 a second per core (`dev_docs/STACKSL_CPU_BACKEND.md`):
30 ms with `parallel = true` on ten cores, 70 ms to 130 ms on one, depending on how many `fbm`
octaves the program has and what else the machine is doing. Compiling and expanding the
template costs 0.35 ms and is noise by comparison. A 600-evaluation search is therefore about
twenty seconds, and the two-arm comparison [`evolveStackSLTowards`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--evolvestacksltowards) runs about forty.

[`evolveStackSLTowards`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--evolvestacksltowards) is the one-call entry point a box wants; see `public/docs/stacksl_evolve.md`.

| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--metric"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">metric</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StackSLMetric</span></code> | What "close to the target" means. See [`StackSLMetric`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt-stackslmetric). |
| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--cache"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cache</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StackSLScoreCache</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Scores already computed for this target, keyed by program text, shared between objectives. |
| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--supersample"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">supersample</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Render each candidate at this multiple of [`dim`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--dim) and average down: 1 (no supersampling) or a power of two. Without it a program can score by aliasing: stripes finer than a fitness pixel, sampled at pixel centres, can land on a pattern that resembles the target at 32 pixels and nothing at 128. Costs `supersample^2` times the render. |
| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--lpipsside"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">lpipsSide</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | The side LPIPS sees. A render smaller than this is enlarged pixel by pixel (and the target with it) before comparison, because AlexNet's deeper stages are 1x1 at 32 pixels. Enlarging adds no detail, it gives the network room to look at the detail the render has. |
| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--lpipsregions"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">lpipsRegions</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Also score LPIPS on each region of an [`lpipsGrid`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--lpipsgrid) by [`lpipsGrid`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--lpipsgrid) tiling of the [`lpipsSide`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--lpipsside) image, as lexicase cases. That is `lpipsGrid^2` more (smaller) LPIPS evaluations per candidate, so off unless you select by lexicase. |
| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--lpipsgrid"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">lpipsGrid</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Regions per side when [`lpipsRegions`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--lpipsregions) is on: 2 is the four quadrants. Each region must be at least [`Lpips.MIN_SIDE`](machine-learning.md#lpips-kt--lpips--min-side) square, so 3 needs an [`lpipsSide`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--lpipsside) of 96. More regions pin *where* and *how many* more tightly; `bands` evolving the right stripes out of phase is what they are for. |
| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--flatfloor"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">flatFloor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolve/#L1202) | What a flat fill of the target's own mean colour would score — the trivial answer's fitness. |

| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--considered"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">considered</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolve/#L1217) | Candidates offered so far, including ones this objective rejected. |
| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--invalid"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">invalid</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolve/#L1221) | Candidates rejected as blank or as a crash. The `failureRate` of `MorphoSearchRun`, here. |
| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--invalidrate"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">invalidRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolve/#L1225) | Fraction of candidates that were not pictures. Reported, never hidden. |
| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--evaluate"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">evaluate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">genome</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StackSLProgram</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Evaluation</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolve/#L1232) | Render `genome` once, score it under both metrics and return the one [`metric`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--metric) asks for. A render that throws, or that the blank guard refuses, scores `INVALID_SCORE` on every case rather than propagating, and is counted in [`invalid`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--invalid). A [`cache`](search.md#stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--cache) hit skips the render. |
| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--render"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">render</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">genome</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StackSLProgram</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">dim</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">this</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">dim</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CpuRaster</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolve/#L1250) | Render `genome` at `dim` — the same call `evaluate` makes, for a caller that wants the pixels. |

| <a id="stackslevolve-kt--stackslimageobjective--scoreat"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">scoreAt</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">genome</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StackSLProgram</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">other</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StackSLTarget</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolve/#L1269) | Fitness of a program against a target at *that* target's resolution, under the same metric. |

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StackSLEvolveRun</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">target</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StackSLTarget</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">evolved</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SearchRun</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">StackSLProgram</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">control</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SearchRun</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">StackSLProgram</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">invalidRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">danglingValues</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">objective</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StackSLImageObjective</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolve/#L1506)

The number a claim is made of. |

## StackSLEvolveStudio.kt { #stackslevolvestudio-kt }

The AI4 chat surface for a [`StackSLEvolution`](search.md#stackslevolution-kt-stackslevolution): [`stackSLEvolveStudio`](search.md#stackslevolvestudio-kt--stackslevolvestudio) registers the `evolve_*`
tools on a box and ties the population to the conversation's branches.

[`stackSLEvolution`](search.md#stackslevolvestudio-kt--stackslevolution) keeps one search on the box, so re-running the box keeps its population.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolveStudio.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolveStudio/)

**Used in:** [Evolving a Shader Toward a Picture](../stacksl_evolve.md)

| --- | --- |
| <a id="stackslevolvestudio-kt--stackslevolvestudio"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">stackSLEvolveStudio</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">evolution</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StackSLEvolution</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;evolve&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLEvolveStudio/#L93) | The StackSL search as a world the AI4 chat works in, the way `ai4_paint_studio` makes a canvas one: the chat runs generations, looks at the leaders, proposes programs of its own, asks the cheap model for a round, takes a gradient step on a literal, and breeds with populations it left behind. |

## StackSLWatchmaker.kt { #stackslwatchmaker-kt }

A language model as a StackSL mutation operator: [`StackSLWatchmaker`](search.md#stackslwatchmaker-kt-stackslwatchmaker) shows a model the target
and the leaders' renders and turns its reply into candidate programs.

The prompt is built by [`StackSLWatchmakerPrompt`](search.md#stackslwatchmaker-kt-stackslwatchmakerprompt), replies are parsed and checked by
[`StackSLProposals`](search.md#stackslwatchmaker-kt-stackslproposals), and [`StackSLModelUsage`](search.md#stackslwatchmaker-kt-stackslmodelusage) sums model calls, tokens and prompt-cache reads.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLWatchmaker.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/stacksl/evolution/StackSLWatchmaker/)

## EyeEvolution.kt { #eyeevolution-kt }

Interactive evolution: a grid of pictures in a box's output panel, where clicking the ones you
like breeds the next generation. The fitness function is the person looking at it.

This is the half of `afield.study.search` that scores nothing itself. `PopulationSearch.kt`
spends a budget of evaluations against an [`Objective`](search.md#populationsearch-kt-objective); this file spends your attention instead.
Both describe a genome with the same [`GenomeOps`](search.md#populationsearch-kt-genomeops), so a genome written for one drives the other
unchanged, and [`breedFrom`](search.md#eyeevolution-kt--breedfrom) is the shared rule for turning a pair of parents into a child.

[`EyeEvolution`](search.md#eyeevolution-kt-eyeevolution) holds the grid, the current parents and every earlier set; [`evolveByEye`](search.md#eyeevolution-kt--evolvebyeye) puts
one in a box and hands it back; [`EyeSetting`](search.md#eyeevolution-kt-eyesetting) is a number the grid's toolbar shows and lets you
turn between generations. Nothing here knows what a genome is beyond the four functions you
supply for breeding it, drawing it, naming it and labelling its tile. In this tree the genome it
is used with is [`afield.lang.rpn.ColorRpn`](search.md#colorrpn-kt-colorrpn), and `ColorRpnEvolution.kt` is the worked example of
wiring one up.

Interactive evolution, where the eye is the fitness function: a grid of tiles in a box's output panel (the parents first, then their children), and clicking [`EyeEvolution.pick`](search.md#eyeevolution-kt--eyeevolution--pick) tiles makes them the next parents and breeds again. This is the loop of Karl Sims' *Genetic Images* and of Dawkins' biomorphs; [`afield.lang.rpn.ColorRpn`](search.md#colorrpn-kt-colorrpn) programs (the madp GA demo) are one genome for it, and any genome with a picture works — StackSL programs, FLines, synth patches drawn as spectra.

## PopulationSearch.kt { #populationsearch-kt }

Population search over *any* genome type — the generic drivers that `alife_evolve.kt`,
`FunctionEvolve.kt` and `afield.simulation.kratos.KratosStudy` all run on. (`afield.lang.morpho.MorphoSearch`
keeps its own.)

A caller supplies two things and nothing else. [`GenomeOps`](search.md#populationsearch-kt-genomeops) says how to make a genome, how to vary
one, and (optionally) how to recombine two; [`Objective`](search.md#populationsearch-kt-objective) says what a genome scored. The five
drivers in [`PopulationSearch`](search.md#populationsearch-kt-populationsearch) then spend a budget of *evaluations* against that pair:
[`PopulationSearch.random`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--populationsearch--random) draws independently and keeps the best, [`PopulationSearch.hillClimb`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--populationsearch--hillclimb)
walks one point, [`PopulationSearch.evolve`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--populationsearch--evolve) runs a (µ+λ) generational loop with tournament or
lexicase selection, [`PopulationSearch.novelty`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--populationsearch--novelty) replaces the objective's own fitness with
distance from an archive of behaviours, and [`PopulationSearch.mapElites`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--populationsearch--mapelites) keeps the best genome
per cell of a grid over the behaviour space rather than one winner.

[`PopulationSearch.random`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--populationsearch--random) is the **control arm**. It draws from exactly the distribution the
other four mutate within, so a difference between their results is a difference in *selection*
rather than in the generator. Reporting an evolutionary result without it says nothing: a
generator good enough to stumble onto a decent genome occasionally looks like a successful
search. `MorphoSearch` reports the same pair for the same reason.

**Budget is evaluations, not generations.** A population of 24 and a hill climb of 1 do very
different amounts of work per generation, so a per-generation budget would compare budgets rather
than methods. [`SearchRun.trace`](search.md#populationsearch-kt--searchrun--trace) is likewise best-so-far *per evaluation*.

**What determinism means here.** Given the same [`GenomeOps`](search.md#populationsearch-kt-genomeops), the same [`Objective`](search.md#populationsearch-kt-objective) and the same
`seed`, a driver returns the same [`SearchRun`](search.md#populationsearch-kt-searchrun): the same best genome, the same trace, the same
evaluation count, every time. It is one seeded `Random` threaded through every draw, and
evaluation is **sequential**, because parallel evaluation would reorder those draws and throw
the property away. It says nothing about thread safety, and it holds only if the caller's
`mutate` and `evaluate` are themselves deterministic functions of their arguments.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/search/PopulationSearch.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/search/PopulationSearch/)

**Used in:** [Spatial artificial life](../alife_examples.md), [Braitenberg vehicles with memory](../braitenberg_vehicles.md)
